frontier.hypothesis: There is a C address tree, other than '&SYM + index' and other than a pointer-local deref, that RTL expand routes to the inline-symbolic MEM form - which would re-open the residual despite the class kill.
frontier.mechanism: The class kill rests on a two-generator model of (mem (plus (reg) (symbol_ref))) validated on four whole-function poles. It has not been validated against every address tree GCC 2.7.2 can build: a const-qualified or differently-typed base, an address that passes through legitimize_address in tools/gcc-2.7.2/config/mips/mips.c because it is initially illegitimate (e.g. an offset too large for the 16-bit field), or a COMPONENT_REF on a symbol-addressed aggregate whose member offset exceeds that field.
frontier.next_probe: Fix the MEM-extraction regex in tmp/grind/func_80062020/s14/gentable.py (it currently misses the nested (plus reg symbol_ref) case, which is why its first run printed '?' for every shape), then extend it into a single-store generator table over ~15 distinct address trees, reading the expand MEM form for each out of in.i.rtl. Any tree that produces the symbolic form from a NON-'&SYM+index' shape is a new lever; feed it into a whole-function epilogue and measure with sandbox.

frontier.hypothesis: The epilogue's 3-insn addressing difference is a build-configuration artefact rather than a C-construct problem - func_80062020 was compiled with a cc1 configuration that differs from the one the rest of text1b.c uses.
frontier.mechanism: The residual is exactly the kind of difference a -G value, PIC/abicalls setting, or cc1 build skew produces: it changes how a symbol+index address is materialised, and it can differ per object without perturbing functions that never form such an address. Fourteen sessions have searched the C side only; the toolchain side has never been swept for this function.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep the honest uniform floor-4 body through the sandbox build across the small set of codegen-relevant cc1 flags that leave the already-matching functions in text1b.c untouched (starting with -G values), and check whether any produces the mixed epilogue. A hit is a build-configuration FINDING to report, not a lever to spend - .claude/rules/no-compiler-divergence.md governs, and the Makefile/engine surfaces are outside the grind session's allowed surface.
